defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A blend tree mixes clips by a value, and a state machine commits to one state.
A transition left at Enabled never fires by itself. Auto does.
An interrupt cuts a state short, and an exit-time transition waits for the clip.
During a cross-fade, the current node already names the new state.
Keep a gameplay fact like the hitbox window on the clip, not in a tween.
A probe checks the body, and a mutation check shows a test can see the bug.
bookends.command: Quiz me on animation terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms blend tree, transition, advance mode, interrupt, exit-time transition, cross-fade, method track, tween, active and recovery. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a game-making situation, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike is wrong.
